prompt: Cities are connected directly or through others. Given which pairs are directly connected, how many separate groups are there?
why: Union each connected pair; the number of distinct roots is the number of groups.
trap: DFS also counts components; union-find shines because the input is a list of pairs.

prompt: A tree had one extra edge added, creating a cycle. Return the edge that can be removed.
why: Process edges in order; the first edge whose ends already share a root is the extra one.
trap: Fast/slow detects cycles in a sequence, not in an undirected graph built from edges.

prompt: Accounts list emails. Two accounts belong to the same person if they share any email. Merge them.
tells: same person if they share any email
why: Union every email in an account together; each final root is one person.
trap: "Merge" sounds like intervals, but there's no ordering, just shared membership.

prompt: Land cells are added to a water grid one at a time. After each addition, report the current number of islands.
why: Each new cell adds an island, then unions with land neighbors; each successful union removes one.
trap: Re-running DFS after every addition is O(cells) each time.

prompt: Given equations like a==b and b!=c, decide whether all of them can be true at once.
tells: all of them can be true
why: Union all == pairs first, then check no != pair shares a root.
trap: Backtracking over assignments is exponential; equality is just grouping.
